fields.label: First VRAM tile reserved for tall text
fields.description: First background tile index (0-255) reserved for tall character tile pairs. Each cached character uses two consecutive tiles from this range. Must not overlap tiles used by the scene background (0 to 191 depending on the scene) or the UI/dialogue tiles (192-255).

fields.label: Last VRAM tile reserved for tall text
fields.description: Last background tile index (inclusive) reserved for tall character tile pairs. The cache holds (range size / 2) characters, at most 64. A two-line dialogue can show up to 36 distinct characters, so reserve at least 72 tiles.

fields.label: Tile placement (VRAM bank)
fields.description: Which VRAM tile data bank the cached character tiles are uploaded to. 'Bank 1 only' and 'Alternate' are Game Boy Color features (Color Only mode, or Color modes running on GBC): they free up or double the bank 0 budget by storing glyphs in bank 1, selected per tilemap cell through attribute bit 3. On DMG hardware the plugin always falls back to bank 0. Alternate placement doubles the characters a given tile range can hold.

fields.label: Enable character tile cache
fields.description: When enabled, rendered tile pairs are tracked in an LRU cache so a character that was already drawn reuses its pair instead of consuming a new one. Disable it to compile the cache out: every character is then rendered into the next tile pair of the reserved range, cycling round-robin. That reclaims all of the cache WRAM (3 bytes per entry) and skips the lookup, but each character is re-uploaded on every use and the reserved range must be large enough for all characters visible at once (two tiles each), otherwise tiles still on screen get overwritten.

fields.label: Character cache capacity (entries)
fields.description: Maximum number of characters the tile-pair LRU cache can track. Each entry costs 3 bytes of WRAM and, when in use, two consecutive VRAM tiles from the reserved range. The usable entry count at runtime is the smaller of this value and (reserved tile range / 2). Lower it to reclaim WRAM, raise it only alongside a larger reserved tile range. Ignored when the character tile cache is disabled: the whole reserved range is then used.

fields.label: Replace stock text rendering
fields.description: Compile GB Studio's own text renderer out of the ROM and point everything that used it at this plugin instead. The stock Display Dialogue, Display Text and Menu events then draw in 16px-tall text, without being replaced by this plugin's own events. Two things follow. Tiles 204-255, which the stock renderer used as its scratch buffer, are free: they can be added to this plugin's reserved tile range with nothing left to collide with. Menus are handled separately and need none of this: the plugin always supplies the menu driver, so its own Menu event works whether this is on or off.

fields.label: Menu cursor row
fields.description: Which tile of a menu line the cursor sits on. A line of this plugin's text is two tilemap rows tall, so the cursor can go beside the top half or the bottom half of it. The lower tile sits level with the baseline; the upper one reads as slightly raised. Which looks right depends on where your font puts its glyphs inside the cell, so try both. Only affects menus drawn by this plugin's Menu event, and by the stock Menu event when 'Replace stock text rendering' is on.
